State from the predecessor’s solo construction:

For unit-rate single-spin flips Q on {-1,+1}^n and L=Q+diag(V), a positive trial h=exp(U) defines mu proportional to h², auxiliary flip rates h(x^i)/h(x), and residual R=V+sum_i[h(x^i)/h(x)-1]. The exact conjugation is h^-1 L h=Q^h+diag(R). Write m=E_mu R.

If the heat-bath sampler for mu has an acquired influence matrix C with spectral radius below1, c_i bounds the global coordinate oscillation of R, q_i^max bounds its flip probabilities, and nonnegative b satisfies (I-C^T)b>=c, then

    m <= lambda_max(L) <= m+K,
    K=(1/4)sum_i q_i^max b_i².

The proof bounds gradients of a heat-bath Poisson solution by the contraction matrix, compares Dirichlet forms and applies the variational principle. It assumes no target spectral gap; the auxiliary contraction and global oscillation inputs must actually be earned.

A sparse local logarithmic/Walsh recursion cancels the nonconstant residual through finite order p. For V=s sum_{edges ij}x_i x_j, bounded graph degree and sufficiently small checked coupling s, the certified pressure-density bias is O(s^(2p+2)). The associated transverse-field Hamiltonian has ground energy -n-lambda. This is finite-order Kirkwood–Thomas machinery with a remainder, not a new weak-interaction tractability class. A fixed mu also supports simultaneous later adaptive potential queries through one acquired finite feature vector; changing h changes the sampling law and its validation requirements.

The predecessor reports exact rational algebra/enclosures, small spectral diagnostics and a completed irregular128-spin acquisition at s=0.1: 4,096 separately restarted endpoints and11,939,840 local updates, with a99% conditional confidence contract including burn-in, quantized transitions and numerical bounds. The interval for lambda/128 is [0.00374252066,0.00381151987]. The trial was analytic, not learned; stronger learned-model performance and a best-method advantage were not established.
